short: New pipeline (imagined MEG mapped to listened MEG, then a listened-trained word decoder), but no no-mapping or null-mapping word control, and a shared closed poem set confounds word decoding.
position: The paper changes the decoding route (M06), the training regime (M03) and the recording (M11), all standard against the field, and under-reports its word-level evaluation (M12). Composing an imagined-to-listened mapping with a listened-trained decoder is new only as a pipeline among 112 pattern-matched studies (the authors' earlier mapping decodes nothing), and stays standard because no control passes unmapped imagined MEG or a null-mapping output through the decoder, so the mapping's contribution to word retrieval is not shown. Every participant imagines the same two poems whose 76 words form the candidate set, so poem identity alone lifts ranks above chance; zero-shot holds across subjects, not across stimuli.
